result: GRP UBCs and P079 UBCs exhibit distinct electrophysiological properties. GRP UBCs show excitatory responses mediated by mGluR1 and AMPA receptors, while P079 UBCs show inhibitory responses mediated by mGluR2 receptors. The two subtypes differ significantly in membrane capacitance, excitability, and sag properties.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm these findings, with one reviewer stating 'GRP-driven TDtomato is expressed exclusively in a subset (20%) of ON-UBCs, defined electrophysiologically (excited by mossy fiber afferent stimulation via activation of UBC AMPA and mGluR1 receptors)' and 'UBCs ID'd/tagged by mCitrine expression in Brainbow mouse line P079 is expressed in a similar minority subset of OFF-UBCs defined electrophysiologically (inhibited by mossy fiber afferent stimulation via activation of UBC mGluR2 receptors).' Another reviewer notes 'evidence for the existence of distinct ON and OFF UBC subtypes based on their electrophysiological properties.'

result: The GRP-Cre/Ai9 and P079 transgenic mouse lines label distinct, largely non-overlapping populations of UBCs. GRP labels approximately 20% of ON UBCs (mGluR1+) and P079 labels approximately 70% of OFF UBCs (calretinin+). These populations have different anatomical distributions and soma sizes in the cerebellum.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm these characterization findings. One reviewer summarizes 'GRP-driven TDtomato is expressed exclusively in a subset (20%) of ON-UBCs...immunocytochemically by their expression of mGluR1' and notes the P079 line labels OFF-UBCs 'immunocytochemically by their expression of Calretinin.' Another reviewer states the study 'provided evidence for the existence of distinct ON and OFF UBC subtypes based on their...anatomical characteristics, and expression patterns of mGluR1 and calretinin in the cerebellum.'

result: A subset of P079 UBCs unexpectedly express mGluR1 (61.3% in cerebellum), distinguishable by lower mCitrine fluorescence intensity and smaller soma size. This finding limits the specificity of the P079 line for OFF UBCs.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding explicitly. One reviewer notes 'such mCitrine expression was also detected in some mGluR1 positive UBCs, which may not have shown up electrophysiologically because of the weaker fluorophore expression without antibody amplification.' This observation is treated as a valid finding that affects the interpretation of the P079 line's specificity.

result: The expression patterns of GRP and P079 UBCs in the dorsal cochlear nucleus mirror those in the cerebellum, with similar proportions of mGluR1+ and calretinin+ cells and similar overlap of P079 with mGluR1 expression.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about these dorsal cochlear nucleus findings. The data is presented as parallel to the cerebellar findings and is implicitly accepted as part of the overall characterization of these mouse lines.

result: Anatomical evidence demonstrates that UBCs form synaptic connections with other UBCs, including all permutations: ON-to-ON, ON-to-OFF, OFF-to-ON, and OFF-to-OFF connections. These connections were visualized using fluorescent labeling and confocal microscopy.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm these connectivity findings. One reviewer states 'Confocal analysis of crossed lines of mice (GRP X P079) stained with antibodies to mGluR1 and calretinin documented the existence of all possible permutations of interconnectivity between cells (ON-ON, ON-OFF, OFF-OFF, OFF-ON).' Another reviewer notes the study 'showed that UBCs of the same subtype provide input to one another' and that there are 'synaptic connections between the ON and OFF UBC subtypes.'

result: The abundance of UBC-to-UBC connections is low and their density could not be accurately quantified due to sparse labeling. Electrophysiological evidence suggests these connections are not common, though prior studies report varying estimates.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this limitation explicitly. One reviewer notes 'their overall abundance was low, and neither their absolute or relative abundance was quantified.' This is treated as an accepted limitation of the anatomical approach rather than a criticism of the findings.

result: Computational modeling demonstrates that feed-forward UBC circuits transform presynaptic signals in distinct ways: ON-to-ON circuits produce extended bursts, ON-to-OFF circuits produce extended pauses, OFF-to-ON circuits produce delayed pauses, and OFF-to-OFF circuits produce delayed bursts.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the modeling results. One reviewer states 'A computational model (NEURON) indicated that the presence of an intermediary UBC (in a polysynaptic circuit from MF to UBC to UBC) could prolong bursts (MF-ON-ON), prolong pauses (MF-ON-OFF), cause a delayed burst (MF-OFF-OFF), cause a delayed pause (MF-OFF-ON) relative to solely MF to UBC synapses.' The modeling is treated as rigorous and the conclusions are accepted.

result: The authors propose that UBC circuits could provide mechanisms for maintaining sensory representations of movement for seconds, diversifying granule cell firing patterns, and contributing to motor learning and adaptive behavior.
evaluation: Reviewers note these functional interpretations require further validation. The editor states 'some in vivo work remains to be conducted in order to test whether the hypothesis and predictions translate into the behaving animal and how it would impact the processing of feedback or feed-forward activity that would be required to promote behavior.' This indicates the functional claims are speculative and need experimental support.
